text:
Rachel: Heads-up  vendor LatAmAnalytics S.A. de C.V. sent an invoice to Redwood, says we should gross-up for a 10% Mexican ISR withholding. They didn't charge VAT. Any quick guidance before I reply? :thinking:

Omar: Do not gross-up by default. Who is the invoiced Redwood entity? That will affect whether Mexican WHT even applies.

Rachel: Invoice shows payee: Redwood, Inc. (US). Snippet from the PDF attached in Coupa:```
Invoice: 2026-06-10-LA
Supplier: LatAmAnalytics S.A. de C.V.
RFC: LAA850101XXX
Amount: USD 14,200
Description: Data labeling & analytics services (remote)
Vendor note: "Please gross-up 10% to cover Mexican withholding tax (ISR) so supplier receives net amount after withholding."
```

Sunita: Quick tax note: Mexican ISR WHT typically arises when a Mexican payer pays a non-resident, or where Mexican-source income rules apply. If Redwood, Inc. (US) is the payer, Mexican WHT is usually not triggered. Also, W-8/W-9 are US forms: a Mexican supplier would submit a W-8BEN-E to a US payer if they want to claim treaty benefits, not a W-9.

TaxTeam: Exactly. Our standard approach: we don't gross-up unless there's a contract clause or an explicit legal requirement. Ask vendor for: (1) the legal basis from Mexican tax authority showing ISR applies to this cross-border payment from a US payer, (2) a Mexican tax assessment or official notice, (3) a copy of the contract clause that requires gross-up if they claim commercial entitlement, and (4) confirm the actual Redwood legal entity that received the services.

Omar: Also request they provide a W-8BEN-E if they are a non-US entity and want treaty relief, or confirm their US tax status if they claim US nexus. If they insist we should withhold, they must give instructions for remittance and paperwork to reclaim any overpayment locally.

Rachel: Draft reply I plan to send: "Thanks  we cannot gross-up by default. Please provide official Mexican tax documentation supporting your ISR claim and attach any contract clause requiring gross-up. Alternatively, please confirm your tax residency and provide a W-8BEN-E if you are a non-US entity claiming treaty benefits. Payment will be placed on hold until validated." Thoughts?

Sunita: Looks good. Add: ask them to reissue the invoice specifying the invoiced legal entity (Redwood, Inc.) and the VAT/tax treatment. That makes it easier for AP to route.

TaxTeam: If vendor provides a Mexican tax notice showing an obligation even when paid by a US company, escalate to Legal for review. But operationally, we hold and do not gross-up absent documentation or contractual obligation.

Omar: I've flagged AP to HOLD the invoice. invoice-bot, set status.

invoice-bot: Payment status updated: ON HOLD for invoice 2026-06-10-LA set by Omar  reason: awaiting vendor tax documentation.

Rachel: Thanks all  will send note now and paste vendor reply in this thread when it comes back.
